evidence.note: Explicit TaskCreate of three ordered milestones: build model.py API, copy to model_optimized.py + benchmark to confirm correctness passes, then run ≤8 optimization experiments keeping fastest passing. This encodes the correct correctness-then-optimization phase gate with done-conditions.

Milestone 1&2 executed in order: write model.py, parity check (62), fix + re-run parity (65-68), only then copy to model_optimized.py and benchmark baseline (71) before marking complete — parity established before any optimization.

Optimization treated as a bounded sequence of six discrete, individually-named experiments (compile, max-autotune, cached masks, hoisted invariants, batched vision, cudagraphs), each benchmarked and logged to results.tsv, stopping at exp6 within the ≤8 budget — discrete experiments not open-ended tinkering.

Final verification re-checks model.py checkpoint correctness and shim wiring; all optimization edits (113,120,128,141-187) targeted only model_optimized.py, so the frozen correctness checkpoint was protected throughout.

reasoning: The agent laid out explicit, ordered, independently-checkable milestones (API build → parity verified → checkpoint copied → bounded optimization) via TaskCreate and honored them, with the correctness checkpoint frozen and each of six optimization attempts scoped as a distinct hypothesis inside the ≤8 budget — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the optimization experiments were designed adaptively one-by-one rather than pre-planned as a coherent risk-ordered search, and there is no evidence of ordering the API implementation by hardest-to-parity components first.
